kind: scope correction to a study inference
original_claim: Over a Z-torsion-free target every such ring map preserves the full divided-power structure.
correction: Torsion-freeness plus M forces B_n=A^[n-1]B1 and hence the variable PD identities. Full scalar PD preservation additionally requires u to preserve the scalar PD ideal, or J=(t)_PD. The identity on Z[epsilon]/epsilon^2 with t=0, source ideal(epsilon), target ideal0 is a counterexample to the unrestricted assertion.

kind: scope of the free B parameters
original_claim: Over an F_p-algebra the B values are free on B_(p^m).
correction: The p-power values freely parametrize derivations solving M; maps of the whole simplicial differential ring must still satisfy the independent coefficient-annihilator conditions. For automorphisms over odd characteristic those conditions force B=0.

original_claim: The condition on B disappears when 2 is invertible; the F3 witness is called reduced.
correction: For A=0,B3=T^[5],others0 over S=F3{T}, all required conditions hold and the map has a nonzero odd image. The ground ring F3 is reduced; S itself is not, since (T^[5])^2=252T^[10]=0. A regular element in the coefficient ideal together with invertible2 is a sufficient replacement forcing B=0.
status: Refuted; exact witness and sufficient replacement proved

original_claim: The unrestricted arrays on scan178 give an affine automorphism scheme.
correction: For continuous maps and for natural coefficient-ring families, only c_m=B_(2^m) are free, they are2-torsion, and c_m tends to0 in total weight. The B functor is the product over output monomials of finite-support input rows, an ind-affine functor rather than an affine scheme. The A coefficients have no2-torsion restriction.
status: Refuted; exact functor and law proved

original_claim: A fixed-ring abstract automorphism of the completed algebra is implicitly determined by the same convergent one-variable data.
correction: Continuity is not automatic for abstract maps: the F2 ultrafilter automorphism fixes polynomial forms but is discontinuous, and its square is identity in dimension1 but not dimension2. Its degree-zero substitution is nevertheless automatically continuous. Natural families over all coefficient algebras are exactly the continuous automorphisms.
status: Abstract reading refuted; both precise categories distinguished

original_claim: Only necessity of invertible determinant is proved on the page.
correction: Invertible Delta gives the inverse continuous substitution by the complete total-weight filtration, followed by a finite inverse in exterior degree. The converse also holds for abstract differential-algebra endomorphisms because their degree-zero parts are forced substitutions.

original_claim: Omega acts on full completed cohomology only through Delta.
correction: The full action is coefficient substitution u=phi0 on product-weight cohomology and is u-semilinear. A=X+X^[2] overZ has Delta1 but acts nontrivially already on the point, T maps to T+T^[2]. Only the associated-weight action is Delta^w, with lowest weight Delta^i in cohomological degreei. All components changing exterior degree vanish.

original_claim: Each positive operation from H^i is decided by its value on Delta[i+1]/boundary.
correction: For i>0 that sphere has H^i=0, so it cannot test such an operation. Sq1 on the degree-one class of RP2 is nonzero, while this sphere test sees zero. Linear cycle-object maps, and finite skeleta of universal K(F2,i), give the valid proof and detection method.
status: Refuted; finite RP2 certificate and correct method supplied

original_claim: The tau-omega programme can be read without specifying the retained category or the uncertain completion hat.
correction: Use an explicit graded-S Serre quotient and strict natural differential-ring maps in that category; only exterior grading is forgotten. Completion has the same homogeneous pieces, whose graded direct sum is the quotient input. These automorphisms induce only identity overF2; no assertion classifies derived-only natural transformations. Original scan182 visually confirms the ambient category.

kind: G is a monoid, with its units determined separately
original_claim: The rescaling parameter may be read as an additive or ordinary multiplicative group without the substitution law.
correction: The full object is S with lambda star mu=lambda(T)mu(Tlambda(T)); its polynomial units are exactly the ordinary ring units S^*. The completed units are precisely series with invertible constant coefficient. This respects the author's explicit correction from group to monoid.

original_claim: The displayed coefficient list for G intersect H leaves its group law unspecified.
correction: G intersect H=1+Ann(T), with Ann(T)=direct sum of (i+1)-torsion k in weighti, and Ann(T)^2=0. Its law is addition. Use a product in the completion. The intersection is trivial exactly when k is additively torsion free.
status: Exact multiplication and torsion scope proved

original_claim: The displayed semidirect decompositions of endomorphism monoids, including the torsion-free coefficient reading, hold.
correction: The coefficient image from G consists of f(T)=sum f_nT^[n] with f_n in nk; T+T^[2] overZ is omitted despite torsion-freeness. Even overQ the scalar-zero endomorphism A=X(T-X),B=0 cannot factor through the unique scalar-zero rescaling. The correct split statement is for automorphism groups using the coordinatewise section for a coefficient substitution.
status: Refuted; corrected split group extension proved

original_claim: Operations induced by Omega lie in Breen's algebra and not in the Steenrod algebra.
correction: The coefficient-fixed action is identity, which is the unit in both algebras. Breen's P0 is Frobenius, distinct from its unit. Full weighted coefficient substitution is semilinear; lowest-weight Delta^i is not a stable operation when Delta is not1. No nontrivial positive operation is produced for exclusive placement.
status: Exclusive claim refuted; exact operation range proved
